title: Contracts + Ownership Review
story: You've learned the two pillars of XIOM safety — contracts for logic and ownership for memory. Now practice using both together in real functions.
why: Mastering the combination of contracts and ownership is the capstone skill of L4 — it's what makes XIOM code provably correct and provably safe.
analogy: Contracts are the blueprint — they say what the building must look like. Ownership is the building code — it ensures the structure won't collapse.
try_it: Write fn 'safe_swap' that takes &mut Vec[Int] and two indices, with requires for valid indices and ensures for the swap result. Test edge cases.
tips: Start with requires (validate inputs), then choose & or &mut (access pattern)
Add ensures to verify correctness of the output and side effects
Every public function should have both contracts AND correct ownership annotations
Think of requires/ensures as 'logic safety' and &/&mut as 'memory safety'
common_mistakes: Writing ensures without testing — ensures should match the actual behavior
Using owned parameters when & would work — be precise about your access needs
Forgetting that @pre refers to values BEFORE the function runs
